messages:
Alex: FYI customer reported daily usage charts shifted by 8 hours, causing day-boundary to fall at 16:00 local. CSV exports show same shift. Billing reported spike because requests counted on previous day.
Priya: thanks — can you paste the account id and a screenshot of the chart + CSV excerpt? also which timezone they expect (PST/PDT?)
Alex: account: acct_9k2l. Screenshot attached (see export name: usage_acct_9k2l_2025-11-12.csv). Customer says they expect charts in America/Los_Angeles (PDT) but platform shows UTC day boundaries.
customer_acct_admin: Confirming — our org is on PDT and all daily reports should use local midnight. Exports breaking finance reconciliations.
Priya: repro steps from support side: 1) open Console -> Usage -> select date range 2025-11-12 to 2025-11-13 2) click Export CSV 3) inspect timestamp column, many entries stamped 2025-11-11T23:xx:xxZ (should be 2025-11-12 local).
Priya: quick check — API call to metrics service used aggregation window: "daily" but we may be feeding UTC boundaries. Can someone from eng-platform triage? @Maria
Maria: looking. initial guess: the metrics aggregator aggregates in UTC and Console applies a timezone transform when rendering charts, but export pipeline pulls the raw aggregated bucket start timestamp and writes it unchanged. that would misalign CSV day boundary.
Josh: is this affecting only exports or also the UI charts? customer said UI charts also look shifted.
Maria: good point. I see two pathways: (A) UI client-side tz conversion bug (old code path) and (B) backend aggregation buckets. i'll diff runtime.
SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2025-2543 - "daily-usage-day-boundary-mismatch" assigned to eng-platform.
Noah: billing team seeing reconciliations for acct_9k2l; we need a temporary mitigation (flag or note) before fix. if we re-run export with proper tz it may reconcile.
Priya: quick mitigation: advise customer to set "timezone=UTC" in export query to align with counts OR we can re-export with server-side conversion. will coordinate with eng.
Maria: found repro: query used by export: 
```SELECT date_trunc('day', bucket_start) AS day, sum(token_count) as tokens
FROM usage_buckets
WHERE account_id = 'acct_9k2l' AND bucket_start >= '2025-11-11'::timestamptz
GROUP BY 1
```
This truncates to UTC day. proper flow should be date_trunc('day', bucket_start AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles').
Maria: root cause: metrics ingestion stores bucket_start in UTC (intended), but export job assumed bucket_start was already localized for account's tz. UI has a client-side convert for charts, but export is server-side and missed conversion.
Alex: can we patch quickly? even a job that rewrites CSV timestamps for exports per-account tz?
Maria: plan: short-term patch in export worker to apply account.tz when serializing timestamp (deploy change + run re-export for affected accounts). long-term: normalize export pipeline to always include both bucket_start_utc and localized_day fields.
Priya: ok i'll ask customer if re-export acceptable and get permission to re-run exports for last 7 days.
Noah: billing: please include a note with the re-export indicating old CSV had UTC buckets — we'll reprocess invoices after we get corrected CSVs.
Josh: need a public-facing blurb? maybe a short Console banner: "Usage exports previously used UTC day-boundaries; corrected exports will be available for affected accounts." low risk but keep customers informed.
Maria: small snippet of proposed patch in node worker: 
```const tz = account.timezone || 'UTC';
const localDay = moment.utc(bucket_start).tz(tz).startOf('day').format();
writeRow({ day: localDay, tokens: sum });
```
Will submit PR, add unit test for America/Los_Angeles boundary behavior.
Priya: customer approved re-export for 2025-11-05 -> 2025-11-12. please mark as priority.
Maria: PR created: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4312 - adds tz-aware export, adds both utc_day and local_day columns to CSV.
SupportBot: Deploy staged to canary (staging) at 1749042000 by ci/deploy-bot.
Alex: can we also backfill UI charts? if UI already correct then no need. customer said both charts+CSV were off — we should verify UI after patch.
Maria: verified UI chart bug was from stale client caching for this account; cache cleared and charts now align with localized days. only export bug remained.
Priya: communicated to customer, re-exported files delivered, customer confirmed numbers reconcile. :party:
Josh: please add a short postmortem note to incidents and tag billing & product.
Alex: thanks team. closing thread after postmortem added. :thumbsup:
